faq.a: Aliyu is associated with the Arabic form عَلِيّ, whose core sense is aliyu; exalted (hausa form).

faq.q: What is the origin of Aliyu?
faq.a: Aliyu is associated with Arabic. Aliyu is the Hausa form of Arabic عَلِيّ (ʿAlī), meaning 'exalted'.
Yes — the underlying form عَلِيّ is Arabic.
Aliyu can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Aliyu should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. The root ع ل و is Quranic; ʿAlī is not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Aliyu mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Aliyu is rendered علی and carries the sense علی، والا.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Aliyu, aliyu. Script forms are علي, علی, عَلِيّ, अली.

faq.q: Is Aliyu a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
